About

Craig Delmont Goss, 70, of Canton, Georgia, passed away on September 23, 2026, surrounded by the love of family and friends. He was born on April 16 in Kennesaw, Georgia, to Carolyn Lynch.

Craig developed an early love of the outdoors while growing up around Allatoona Lake in Bartow County, Georgia. He loved to hunt and fish, and he passed that knowledge, appreciation, and love of nature down to his sons.

Craig had a natural gift for craftsmanship and began working with stone at a young age, laying masonry for his stepfather's company. That early experience eventually helped lead him to Red Top Mountain State Park, where he worked as a lead contractor and took on some of the park's more complicated construction projects. He helped build cabins throughout the park, including a breezeway cabin that still stands there today. His work at Red Top became an important part of his life and is a lasting example of the skill and care he brought to everything he built.

Over time, Craig expanded his craftsmanship from stone into woodworking and homebuilding. He became exceptionally skilled with wood and eventually turned that talent into a career, building homes and taking on remodeling projects of his own.

One of the highlights of his career came while working in Bridgemill, where he was selected to build a home on the neighborhood's prestigious "Street of Dreams." The project gave him the opportunity to work alongside some of the area's top builders and craftsmen, with the freedom to showcase his own creativity, design sense, and attention to detail. It was the kind of challenge Craig was built for, and he took great pride in creating something that could stand alongside the best work in the community.

Craig will be remembered for his love of the outdoors, his craftsmanship, his independence, his sense of humor, and the knowledge he shared with the people around him. He had a way of teaching by doing, and much of what he knew and loved continues on through his family.

His family is deeply grateful to everyone who cared for him, supported him, visited him, called, prayed, and shared their love throughout his life.
